title: Duchy of Jawor
capsule: The Duchy of Jawor was a Piast appanage in Lower Silesia carved out of the fragmented duchy of Wrocław in the late 13th century, with its seat at Jawor (German: Jauer). It was ruled by a junior Piast line including Bolko I of Jawor, who built castles at Bolków and Grodno and patronized Cistercian monasteries as counterweights to Bohemian expansion. The duchy merged with neighboring Świdnica by 1314 under the combined Duchy of Świdnica-Jawor and eventually passed by inheritance to the Bohemian Crown in 1392.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Territorial limits are reconstructed from Silesian Piast partition documents; boundaries between closely related appanage duchies shifted frequently and cartographic precision is limited.
